highlights.title: Themed alarm sounds and spoken alerts
changes: Alarms now use themed Acoustic/Electronic sets with Mild/Medium/Harsh intensity and voice alerts.
Every alarm now defaults to Acoustic Medium and previous tones are moved into an "Other Sounds" group.

includedPullRequests.title: Rework Trio Alarm Sounds: Add Urgency Levels and Voice Alarms
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Replaces the generic alarm tone list with sound sets written for each individual alarm, in three intensity levels, plus spoken alerts. Every alarm now defaults to the Acoustic Medium set, and the previous tones move into a collapsed "Other Sounds" group.

The complaints that prompted this were about Critical device alerts being too disruptive, but the underlying problem was broader:  tone choice was secretly a volume control. The bundled tones ranged from `critical.caf` at -1.2 dBFS RMS to `high_chimes.caf` at -30.4, a 29 dB spread, with every file peaking at full scale. Picking "Critical" instead of "High Chimes" was a 29 dB jump that nothing in the UI hinted at, and the default for the Critical device tier was one of the loudest files we had. 

## The New Sounds

This PR proposes new sound sets for Trio's alarms – Urgent Low, Low, Low Glucose Soon, High, Carbs Required, Device Critical and Device Time-Sensitive – in two themes, Acoustic and Electronic, at three intensity levels, Mild, Medium, Harsh, plus a spoken set in two voices. These new sounds were designed for us by an anonymous diabetes dad and trio user who also didn’t like the default sounds. 

Intensity is carried by timbre, loudness and length together, so each level is its own recording rather than one recording at three gain settings. Rising and falling pitch tracks glucose direction, and the sets share a voicing so they read as coming from the same app.

Defaults move to Acoustic Medium everywhere, which is what we recommend after hallway testing with adult and child PwDs and caregivers.

## Picker

Opening Tone on an alarm now shows a "For This Alarm" section first — Acoustic, Electronic and Voice, written for that alarm — with the previous 18 tones and 8 new one-offs collapsed under "Other Sounds". The group auto-expands when the current selection lives inside it, so a pick is never hidden behind a closed group.

Selecting Acoustic or Electronic reveals an Urgency Level slider; selecting Voice reveals an Amy/Bryce control. Both audition on change, since the point is hearing how the character differs.

Purpose-written sets are scoped to the alarm they were written for and do not appear elsewhere. The Normal device tier has no set of its own and shares the Time-Sensitive one, the gentler of the two device sets.

## Recording
Simulator recordings do not carry sound, so this is just to display the new UI. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/087a40b3-d028-49ad-a102-c6984a33413b

## Licensing

Adds `ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md`. The spoken alerts were generated with Piper:

- **Bryce** — public domain, credited as a courtesy.
- **Amy** — the Piper model card points at `MycroftAI/mimic3-voices`, which is **CC BY-SA 4.0**. Attribution and share-alike apply to those audio files; Trio's own licence is unaffected. The file records that the clips were looped, since CC BY requires changes to be indicated.
